title: Ingram Sheets
pitch: A spreadsheet whose engine runs in your browser and publishes twelve tools to whichever agent is driving the tab. Spreadsheets for models, not models for spreadsheets.
about_excerpt: A spreadsheet whose engine runs in your browser and publishes twelve tools to whichever agent is driving the tab. Spreadsheets for models, not models for spreadsheets. Like Comment Story Updates What it is Ingram Sheets is a spreadsheet whose calculation engine runs in the browser. It publishes its operations to whichever agent is driving the tab: read a range, write a block, extend a pattern, format, restructure, undo, point at a cell. ChatGPT supplies the model; we supply the sheet and hold no inference key. Why it needs WebMCP The engine is IronCalc compiled to WebAssembly, holding the live workbook in memory. There is no server-side copy of the sheet you are looking at: nothing that could recalculate it remotely, no endpoint that knows where your cursor is. An agent outside the tab has nothing to call. Spreadsheets for models, not models for spreadsheets The engine keeps every intermediate result at a stable address, so the model writes D17 instead of recopying a value it can transcribe wrong. It owns the dependency graph, so the model declares one local relation at a time and the engine keeps the global result consistent. And every write returns the cells whose computed values changed, recalculation ripple included. That return value is the tool contract: the model is corrected at each edit rather than at the end of a script, and it can skip the read that would otherwise confirm what it just did. Working alongside it Person and agent are in the same document at the same time. The agent's writes recalculate on screen, its focus moves across the grid in its own colour, and it can highlight a range and attach a note. Edit a cell while it works and your change is attached to its next tool result, so it re-plans against the current sheet. A code interpreter cannot do this. Its state ends with the session and its output is not editable. In a workbook every intermediate value sits next to the formula that produced it, and whoever knows the discount rate is wrong fixes the cell. How it is built Twelve tools, generated from the Zod schemas that also drive the built-in chat agent, so the two surfaces cannot drift. Every write goes through one controller, so an outside agent gets the same cursor and highlight behaviour as the built-in one, and its edits ride the same compare-and-swap save as a keystroke. Reads are marked readOnlyHint so the host can run them unattended. The two that return cell contents are marked untrustedContentHint : a cell can hold any text, including text shaped like an instruction, and the agent is told up front that what comes back is data. Results are returned as plain text rather than MCP content blocks, because the host serializes whatever a tool returns and the wrapper reaches the model as JSON noise around the grid. Prior work and hackathon work Ingram Sheets is a pre-existing project. WEBMCP.md in the repository separates what shipped before the submission period from what was built during it, with the commit history. Trying it Open https://sheets.ingram.tech/try in the ChatGPT desktop app's built-in browser, on GPT-5.6 Sol or Terra. No sign-in. The panel on the right logs every tool call with its result.
